title: Direct original Native versus current product Native comparison cases
purpose: Run corresponding original production operations against independent 570 and current candidate state and preserve the observable result, effect, and failure evidence.

baseline.candidate_feature_policy: Cargo default production plus explicit memory-provider-host and semantic-fastembed; attestation records this effective ordered set
baseline.build_command: reference: cargo build -p tracedecay-cli --bin tracedecay --features test-transport; candidate: cargo build -p tracedecay-cli --bin tracedecay --features memory-provider-host,semantic-fastembed
baseline.source_policy: the reference source is read-only; the runner does not copy original implementation code, algorithms, or responses

historical_audit.status: historical-only; retained for audit context and never used as an execution oracle

invocation.same_logical_input: the request, operation identity, owner and scope fields are equal on both sides; only binary, process, physical state paths and capture paths differ
invocation.separate_state: the runner allocates original/<case> and product/<case> state roots and never copies a database, WAL, journal, receipt, or post-run state between sides
invocation.production_boundary: supported cases invoke an existing tracedecay CLI tool or MCP tools/call route; an external argv is allowed only when the original route is not CLI-exposed and is recorded as such
invocation.reopen: case authors request explicit after and reopened checkpoints; the runner executes reopened checkpoints only after verified owned close and a fresh daemon authority identity
invocation.reference_guard: verify-reference runs before any case and refuses an absent, differently pinned, or dirty 570 reference checkout
invocation.candidate_identity: the product binary SHA-256, full candidate source revision, source root, and build attestation are captured; missing or unknown candidate provenance blocks execution
invocation.root_isolation: source, binary, process, store, project, profile, state, socket, and artifact roots are side-specific and retained in the run and case manifests
invocation.authority: owned MCP actions require an authenticated initialize nativeOriginalActionPrepare acknowledgement followed by tools/call nativeOriginalActionNonce and a runner-verified nativeOriginalActionReceipt; response self-assertions are insufficient
invocation.ncm_oracle: independent_real_worker_conformance; the pinned 570 side has no encoder worker and records an explicit unavailable worker boundary, while the candidate worker is independently attested

cli_tool.description: The shipped CLI tool surface; it reaches the daemon-owned MCP dispatch and retained production composition.

mcp_stdio.description: The existing MCP stdio server. The runner sends initialize, notifications/initialized, and one tools/call request, then closes stdin.

command.description: An explicitly supplied executable argv for a corresponding original production route that has no CLI wrapper. The command and route remain visible in the capture.

outcomes.pass: both sides produced parseable semantic results that agree after only the case-declared reviewed JSON pointer projection
outcomes.fail: the corresponding side status, semantic result, score/order/provenance, durable effect, receipt, or checkpoint differs
outcomes.unknown: the route or result cannot support a comparative conclusion, including an unavailable original route or an unparseable response; raw evidence remains retained
outcomes.unsupported: the route is explicitly unavailable at the selected boundary on both sides; no process or successful empty result is substituted
outcomes.invalid: the case or request violates this contract; invalid input is retained outside the parity denominator
outcomes.censored: the process or host action reached its declared cutoff before a terminal result; elapsed-at-cutoff and raw streams remain evidence
outcomes.cleanup_failure: owned process or daemon cleanup was not verified; the operation is unknown even when its response was parseable
outcomes.errors: a typed production error is compared as a semantic result when both sides expose one; process nonzero alone never becomes success
outcomes.provider_contact_unverified: a child process being spawned does not prove provider contact; only a case-declared composition proof response can establish the selected boundary
outcomes.same_identity_rejected: same binary digest/root, same source root, or unverified process/store ownership cannot form a comparison pair
outcomes.matrix_outcomes: cancelled, partial, effect_unknown, and blocked remain typed outcomes; they are never collapsed into pass or an empty response
outcomes.terminal_mapping: all RetainedOutcomeStatusV1 values map to typed runner outcomes; only recognized completed values can pass and arbitrary nonzero payloads remain unknown

capture.request: request.json contains the exact canonical JSON request sent to the selected route and its SHA-256
capture.stdout: stdout.bin preserves every byte emitted by the child
capture.stderr: stderr.bin preserves every diagnostic byte emitted by the child
capture.process: process.json records argv, cwd, process identity, process group, process root, return code, cutoff, cleanup status, and remaining owned children
capture.side_state: side-specific source, binary, process, store, project, profile, state, socket, and artifact roots are recorded in the run and case manifests; state probes are captured as explicit checkpoints
capture.comparison: comparison is over parsed semantic responses and selected state probes; raw payloads, source refs, receipts, and all stream artifacts remain alongside it
capture.composition: case-level side-specific proof actions must expose required JSON pointers and optional exact values; a spawned process or hardcoded label is not contact/composition evidence
capture.bindings: output_bindings are response-pointer captures scoped independently to original and product; missing bindings are unknown and never substituted
capture.lifecycle: lifecycle.close and lifecycle.reopen evidence records runner-owned daemon identity, endpoint, profile, process exit, and a fresh authority identity; a completed close child response alone is insufficient
capture.overwrite_policy: new run and case directories are created exclusively; an existing artifact directory is refused so a failed run cannot be replaced

rules: skipped, blocked, fallback-only, evidence-missing and unexplained are not pass
record first causal stage before any downstream symptom
reference and candidate artifacts are independently hashed
mutations require effect, receipt and state evidence; reads require explicit no-effect evidence
process and store identities are distinct from binary identities
exact request_digest hashes the canonical request bytes retained in request.json
every readiness row carries an exact matrix binding including operation oracle track profile and evidence shape
Native NCM and semantic tracks require their declared identity fields; missing fields block pass
authority-correlated route and store identity is required; response self-assertion is not authority
mutating attempts require observed checkpoint or fresh reopen evidence; read-only attempts require explicit no-effect evidence
MCP action.tool must equal the published daemon-mapped tool for its route; fact_store variants use tracedecay_fact_store_<action> and cannot be relabelled through the generic dispatcher
receipt-backed requests cannot carry caller-selected session_id, thread_id, conversation, provider-session, agent-session, or task-session selectors; scope is daemon-selected before prepare
digest-bearing action and terminal-result JSON rejects floating-point values until an exact cross-language number canonicalizer is adopted
ledger population rejects unexpected and over-counted rows
run-manifest and case-result are atomically finalized after all observed attempt fields are known

final case-result result_digest hashes canonical newline-terminated content with its own digest and nested ledger-row result_digest fields set to null; the digest is verified when the artifact is read
nested attempt-row result_digest remains null so the append receipt and final case-result digest cannot form a self-referential cycle

readiness.readiness_mode: requires every row in the frozen matrix with its declared oracle and planned run count; --operation is rejected
readiness.comparison_mode: permits focused cases for development but does not claim readiness
readiness.attempt_population_policy: readiness requires all frozen rows, exact binding, and exactly each row.runs.planned observed ledger attempts; missing, unexpected, or over-counted rows are blocked
readiness.case_binding: matrix_binding must exactly repeat matrix_row_id, track, profile, operation, oracle_kind, oracle_case, identity, identity_evidence, effect_receipt_state, required_identity_fields, required_evidence_fields, identity_requirements, and track_identity_requirements; every readiness action must repeat matrix_row_id, matrix_operation, matrix_oracle_case, and matrix_route, with public route translation checked against the frozen row

build_attestation.policy: the attestation must bind the selected executable hash to the full source revision and source root before a run starts

ncm_worker_attestation.required_for: normal NCM worker execution; independent 570 oracle records the reference worker as unavailable
ncm_worker_attestation.policy: runner input is read through a stable non-symlink file; pins are checked against an independently observed native worker, authenticated daemon action receipt, live daemon runtime, and functionality probe

identityRequirement.description: A frozen identity requirement is a non-empty literal, non-empty literal list, or an explicit typed requirement descriptor.

case_schema.title: Native original comparison case
case_schema.description: Schema for one runner case. Runtime validation additionally enforces route, effect, lifecycle, and frozen-matrix rules.

route_semantics.original_native: corresponding 570 Native operation through the direct retained production boundary; compare canonical payload, score/order, effect, receipt, and reopened state
route_semantics.session_lcm: corresponding 570 session/LCM operation through canonical host/session/LCM services; compare coverage, omissions, cursors, raw/payload authority, lineage, effects, and reopened state
route_semantics.host_extension: current product host/storage safety behavior with no fabricated 570 counterpart; original availability is unknown or unsupported and the result is classified separately
route_semantics.state_regression: saved-data, owner, cursor, locator, or restart evidence; classify an absent original counterpart as unknown rather than claiming parity
